results.notes: MAJOR FINDING: docs/08 (and docs/design §7 '~12 days') budget only HX711 1.5 mA and omit the 3.3 mA bridge excitation. Continuous HX711+bridge (4.8 mA) alone already exceeds the 3 mA target, so the 7-day goal is NOT met as designed (~4.2 days). Remedies: (a) power-gate the analogue front-end / PD_SCK sleep and sample in bursts (50% duty -> ~2.5 mA, 7-8 days), (b) 1000 mAh cell, (c) lower bridge excitation. No hardware change is made here.

results.notes: FINDING: with the BOM 4.7k pull-ups and 100 pF bus capacitance, tr(30-70%) ~398 ns > 300 ns -> the intended 400 kHz I2C does NOT meet Fast-mode timing. 200 pF is even worse (~796 ns). Standard-mode 100 kHz passes (<=1000 ns) for all tested cases. Recommendations: (a) run the OLED at 100 kHz, or (b) change R3/R4 to 2.2k (186 ns @100pF; still 373 ns @200pF -> keep bus cap <= ~150 pF and verify with scope). I2C bus capacitance is an ASSUMPTION (module + traces); measure it.

thresholds.source: project battery gauge requirement; ADC leakage NOT specified in local docs -> ASSUMPTION

results.notes: RISK/FINDING: the 100k/100k divider has a 50 kohm Thevenin source; every 0.1 uA of ADC input leakage adds 10 mV at the pin = 20 mV at the battery. At 1 uA the error is ~100 mV (2.4 %). The exact ESP32-S3 ADC leakage is not in the locally available datasheets, so this is a conditional finding: measure it (or calibrate the gauge) before trusting the uncalibrated reading. C13 does not remove DC leakage. Mitigations: factory/field calibration, lower divider (e.g. 10k/10k costs ~210 uA), or a buffered/op-amp divider.

honesty_boundary: All models are behavioural, not chip-level; HX711/DW01A/TP4056/ME6211 die behaviour is approximated from datasheet numbers.
Simulation pass does not imply hardware pass: noise, drift, thermal and I2C timing must be measured on a hand-built board.
Thresholds and assumptions are listed per result; assumptions are labelled.
